as_of: 2026-09-20, orchestrator pass 182 -- a synthesis over the campaign's own findings, no new measurement
headline: Every FUNCTIONAL defect this campaign has found is at a CALL SITE, not inside a kernel. NINE of them as of pass 182. The arithmetic in the ops is right; what is wrong is which argument reaches them, when, and whether they are called at all. The only two things that are not call sites are a precision ceiling (the softmax) and one residual still unattributed (the trunk's backward amplification). The ninth is the cleanest specimen and the largest: `recipes.py` never passes `betas`, so a library default of 0.999 ships where the reference recipe runs 0.95, and correcting it moves the two-step update by 1862x.

the_eight.found_by: of3t-wirefix, pass 182, pre-registered before the arm that measures it
the_eight.note: the largest single factor the campaign has found: on a 40-tensor two-step probe, passing betas=(0.9, 0.95) takes d_2 from 9.095550e-03 to 4.884661e-06, a factor of 1862. Located by ELIMINATION, not by curve-fitting: AdamW.step() is bit-identical to torch.optim.Adam on identical gradients (ratio exactly 1.0 over eight elements spanning 1.0 to 1e-12), the accumulated gradient reaching each optimizer at k=2 is bit-identical (rel 0.000000e+00), the counts match and the rate matches -- identical inputs and identical formula giving a 0.9 % different update leaves only a constant

the_two_that_are_not.why: a genuine precision ceiling inside the op, not a call site. Both device levers were bounded against the training bar and miss by two orders of magnitude; only a host float64 softmax reaches it.

still unattributed. of3t-trunkback returned NO-GO with the locus in the single-track cotangent chain, four candidates tested and four refuted. It may yet turn out to be a call site; it is not counted as one until it is.

why_this_is_worth_stating_rather_than_ju: three of the eight are cases where the LAYER DEFAULT IS CORRECT and the caller overrides or omits it -- so reading the function's signature, or its default, or its tests, tells you nothing. Two more are code that exists, is tested, and is never invoked: `clip_and_accumulate` has three test call sites and zero production ones, and `self.participation` is written and never read. A test suite that exercises a helper directly gives no evidence that the shipped path calls it. The campaign's standing rule -- READ THE CALL SITE, NOT THE DEFAULT -- has now been paid for eight times, and the strongest form is: for a port, the interesting bugs are in the wiring, and the instruments that find them are whole-path ones (§7's trajectory, an end-to-end forward) rather than per-op ones.
the_methodological_consequence: per-parameter gradient equivalence -- the campaign's main instrument, §3, on which most of its effort went -- is structurally blind to all eight. It compares what an op computes from given inputs. Five of these eight change which inputs arrive or whether the op runs. That is why §8 requires §7 as well, and why §7 having never been run was worth catching.

the_eight_RENAMED: this list is now NINE; the key is kept so nothing that indexes it breaks. See `the_count`.
the_pattern_sharpened_at_pass_182: FOUR of the nine are now the same sentence: a value the reference recipe sets in its config, which our recipe never passes, so the library's own default ships instead -- weight_decay, plateau_until, betas, and the participation divisor. None is a wrong number written down anywhere. Each is a number never written down at all, where the fallback happened to be something else. Grepping for the wrong value finds nothing in every one of these cases; only diffing the recipe's ARGUMENT LIST against the reference's config finds them.
